title: Course Schedule: Taking What's Free
summary: Count each course's unmet prerequisites, take courses whose count is zero, and spot the cycle when the queue runs dry.

takeaway.summary: Repeatedly take a node with no incoming arrows and remove its arrows. If the queue empties before every node is taken, the nodes left sit on a cycle.
whenToUse: Tasks with prerequisites: find an order or prove there is none
Detecting a cycle in a directed graph

scenes.narration: Five courses, numbered 0 to 4. An arrow runs from each prerequisite to the course that needs it: 0 before 1 and 4, 1 before 2, 2 before 3, and 3 before 1. Can you finish them all?
scenes.caption: Five courses, with arrows from each prerequisite

scenes.narration: Checking every order of five courses means 120 orders. Instead, count how many prerequisites each course still has, and take any course whose count is zero.
scenes.caption: Checking all 120 orders is slow

scenes.narration: The badge on each course is how many arrows still point into it. Only course 0 has none, so it goes in the queue.
scenes.caption: Badges count unmet prerequisites: only 0 is ready

scenes.narration: Take course 0. Its arrows are used up, so courses 1 and 4 each lose a prerequisite. Course 4 reaches zero and joins the queue; course 1 still waits on 3.
scenes.caption: Take 0: course 4 reaches zero and joins the queue

scenes.narration: Take course 4. Nothing depends on it, and now the queue is empty.
scenes.caption: Take 4: nothing depends on it, and the queue is empty

scenes.narration: Two courses taken out of five. Courses 1, 2, and 3 each wait on another of the three, a cycle, so none of them can ever reach zero. The answer is false.
scenes.caption: Only 2 of 5 taken: 1, 2, and 3 wait on each other

scenes.narration: This is topological sort with Kahn's algorithm: keep taking a node with no incoming arrows. If the queue empties before every node is taken, the rest sit on a cycle. It runs in O(V + E) time.
scenes.caption: Kahn's algorithm: take what's free, and catch cycles
